items.stem: A product owner asks for a fast and accurate answer bot. The team has no number for either word. The team must set a pass or fail check before any design work. Which step meets the constraint?
options: Pick the largest model, and tune the wording until the demo looks accurate.
Enable a workspace spend limit so that the bot stays fast and accurate.
Set a metric, a threshold, and an owner, and add a weekly human panel to score every answer.
Convert fast and accurate into a latency threshold and a task fidelity score, with an owner who signs each threshold.
items.rationale: Task fidelity and latency are common success criteria, and each needs a threshold before design starts. The owner who signs each threshold is general practice. (Inference)
items.trap: The largest model with tuned wording looks productive, but the team then builds toward a bar that nobody measured.

items.stem: A project team needs a monthly spend cap for its own traffic only. The cap must not include traffic from other teams. Which setup meets the constraint?
options: Create a project workspace and a staging workspace, scope each API key, and set a spend limit on each.
Use the Default Workspace with a shared key, and set a spend limit there.
Create a workspace for the project, scope its API key to that workspace, and set a spend limit on it.
Set a per-minute rate limit on the project key, which caps the monthly spend.
items.rationale: A workspace has its own spend limit, and a key scoped to that workspace counts only toward it. The Default Workspace offers no spend limit, so the project needs its own workspace.
items.trap: A spend limit on the Default Workspace looks like the simplest cap, but that workspace accepts no spend limit.

items.stem: A support bot team builds an evaluation set. The team wants a fast check loop and coverage of rare cases from real traffic. Select two actions that meet both requests.
options: Score every answer with a human panel before each test run.
Add edge cases from real traffic to the test set.
Use code-based checks wherever the output format allows them.
Use the workspace spend limit as the pass threshold for each answer.
items.rationale: Code-based checks rank first in speed and reliability in the docs. Test sets should follow the real task mix and include edge cases.
items.trap: A human panel on every answer looks thorough, but the docs call human grades slow and expensive.
